main_text.p: non clandestinis infidijs [?], nec longa morborum asperitate, nec delicatorum fine, sed in medio cursu florentium gloriarum, hunc merui clarum è medio digressum ] sic illa, sed Historici Christiani pænè omnes, eius interitum ad speccialem Dei digitum referunt, quod & ipsum fassum aiunt, cum manante m ex vu[?]nere sanguinem manu exceptum in aerem spargens, exclamarit ; Vicisti Galilæe, vel vt narrat {o}Zonaras :. Satiare Nazarene, vt etiam prædictum erat abAnnal. Tom.3. illo Ludimagistro Antiochinensi, à quo cum per iocum sciscitaretur Libanius, quid rerum tum gereret Fabri filius, cum respondisse memorat Theodoretus [ huius vniuersitatis artifex, quem tu per risum Fabri filium nominas, Iuliano loculum fabricatur. ] Ita perijt Iulia-nus ab hofte, vel ab ipso Deo, non à Christiano milite interfectus; licet interminatus fuerit, si ex Persia Victor redijset Ammianus lib.25. & Chrysost. cont.Gentiles.{p}se omnes & boues, & Christianos suis Dijs pro victima immolatu-rum. {q}Corpus auten iam defunctum, (quia Imperatoris licet perditissimi cadauer ) curatum pro copia rerum &

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "infidijs" (first line, the letters are faint) and "vu!nere" (the middle letter is obscured by a mark in the scan; read as "vulnere"). Long s throughout is rendered as plain s. The note mark "°" in the text is read as {o}, matching the margin note. The right-margin notes read "p Ammianus lib.25. & Chrysost. cont.Gentiles." and "q Ammianus ibidem.". The second note is placed by its mark q in the text before "Corpus", and is recorded in full here: "q Ammianus ibidem." Doubtful readings: "licet" (possibly "licèt") and "cadauer )" with a space before the closing bracket, both copied as they appear. Printed spellings "Dijs", "perijt" and "auten" are left as printed.
